working: extension installs and activates in both browsers

form.submit SUCCEEDS in both browsers: {ok:true, kind:"form.submit", data:{healed:false, ok:true}}
h3State.failing: form.fill returns "A protected or malformed form field was refused." in both browsers.
h3State.sharpenedDiagnosis: This is NOT selector resolution and NOT a permission problem. form.submit succeeds with the SAME selector (#searchbox_input) and the same token, so the element resolves and the origin is granted. The refusal therefore comes from inside fillApprovedFields after resolve() succeeds — either its protectedPattern matching something about the field, or its usable()/ambiguity branch. background.js:264 holds the pattern; the next session should log which branch fires rather than infer it.
h3State.selectorNote: input[name="q"] was the wrong selector and produced the same message for a different reason: DuckDuckGo has several hidden inputs named q, querySelector returned a hidden one, and usable() correctly rejected it. #searchbox_input is the visible field (name=q, id=searchbox_input, aria-label="Search with DuckDuckGo").
h3State.productDefectFixedThisSession: ensureOriginPermission called chrome.permissions.request from inside the message handler, where a service worker has no user activation, so it THREW instead of returning false. That threw past the actionable refusal at background.js:805 and surfaced as the generic catch-all. Now wrapped in try/catch returning false, so the specific message is reachable.
h3State.nextStep: Instrument fillApprovedFields to report WHICH branch refuses, then fix or adjust. Everything else in the H3 chain is proven working.

h4State: NOT STARTED. Needs navigation confirmed via extension events, a deliberately slow-loading element, multiple tabs without cross-talk, and one real approved upload and download. The harness already records CDP events, which is what navigation confirmation should read.

Protected-field refusal is already proven at protocol level by the zero-touch harness executing the real background.js: the pattern at background.js:205 and :264 covers password, otp, 2fa, captcha, cvv, card, iban, ssn, pin and recovery. Restart-reconnect and planted-failure detection have no coverage yet.

environmentNotes.headlessCannotGrantPermissions: Under --headless=new the extension consent prompt is auto-denied and chrome.permissions.request returns false. H3 onwards must run headful. Measured, not assumed.
environmentNotes.loadExtensionFlagIsDead: --load-extension is ignored by Chrome 137+ and by Edge. CDP Extensions.loadUnpacked with --enable-unsafe-extension-debugging is the working route and needs no policy change.
environmentNotes.serviceWorkerStateIsVolatile: pairingCode and pairingToken are module-level state in an MV3 service worker. Pair immediately before use; anything that waits for a real site to load will find the worker restarted and the pairing gone.
environmentNotes.originPinningIsReal: externally_connectable pins to caeracadane.com, localhost and 127.0.0.1. A controlled site cannot message the extension — the controlling origin and the controlled tab are deliberately different, and the extension acts on a tab named by tabId.

noOwnerActionRequired: Unlike the earlier browser-control blocker, nothing here waits on the owner. H3-H5 are ordinary remaining work.
h3Resolution: The refusal was mine: fillApprovedFields rejects any field where typeof field.name !== "string" using the SAME message as a genuinely protected field. Adding name fixed it. H3 now proven on Wikipedia classic skin in both browsers, navigating Main_Page -> /wiki/XML.
h5DesignConflict: H5 asks for reconnection "without manual re-pairing". The extension deliberately does the opposite: chrome.runtime.onSuspend sets pairingToken = null, commented "a new session must pair again". That is a security decision -- the popup is the user-presence factor, and a token surviving a restart would be a standing grant nobody re-consented to. What is proven is the honest version: the stale token is REJECTED after restart, and a fresh pairing re-establishes control immediately with no reinstall. The requirement was not met by weakening the extension.
